lists.title: List assignment
lists.question: What will print(a) display?
lists.explanation: b = a gives b its own copy of the list, separate from a. The call b.append(4) adds 4 to the end of the list that b refers to. Since only b was modified, print(a) displays [1, 2, 3].
claims: b = a gives b its own copy of the list.
b.append(4) adds 4 to the end of the list that b refers to.
lists.evidence: When you assign a list to a variable, the variable refers to the existing list.
lists.transfer_question: Keep the original list unchanged and include all three attendees in updated. Which line should replace the comment?
lists.transfer_code:
original = ["Rina", "Maya"]
# Add one line here.
updated.append("Sam")
lists.debrief: Assignment gives both names the same list. print(a) displays [1, 2, 3, 4]. In the application question, updated = original[:] starts with the original names in a new outer list, so appending preserves the original.

range.title: Loop boundaries
range.question: Which numbers will be printed, in order?
range.explanation: range(2, 5) starts at 2. The range includes its stop value, so this loop prints 2, 3, 4, and 5 in order.
range.evidence: The given end point is never part of the generated sequence.
range.transfer_question: A report should include exactly pages 8 through 11, including both endpoints. Which expression should replace PLACEHOLDER?
range.debrief: The stop value is excluded. The loop prints 2, 3, 4. To include pages 8 through 11, use range(8, 12).

division.title: Integer floor division
division.question: What will Python print?
division.explanation: With two integer inputs, // returns an integer. It always drops the fractional part toward zero. Here the mathematical quotient is about -2.33, so Python prints -2.
claims: With two integer inputs, // returns an integer.
division.evidence: For integer operands, floor division applies the mathematical floor to the quotient. Floor is the greatest integer less than or equal to that quotient. (Paraphrase)
division.transfer_question: A map groups coordinates into tiles of width 5. Which tile number will this code assign to x = -1?
division.debrief: Python floors the quotient. -7 // 3 is -3, and -1 // 5 is -1. Both results round down to the next lower integer.
